title: Code Refit: Eval Harness and Prompt Inventory
body:
Purpose and scope:
This working doc describes the "refit" evaluation harness for onboarding new code-generation and refactoring models into Redwood’s serving pipeline. The goal is to produce a small-but-high-fidelity corpus and an automated regression harness that tests three dimensions: correctness (compilation + unit tests), behavioral fidelity (preserve intended semantics), and style/maintainability (linters, code health heuristics).

Intended audience:
- Applied ML engineers building onboarding pipelines
- Solutions engineers evaluating model suitability for customer workloads
- Release engineers who will integrate regression checks into CI

High level requirements (must have for a model to pass onboarding):
1) Static build pass: generated/refactored outputs should compile in target language(s) for >= 90% of test cases in the corpus for the stable channel.
2) Unit test parity: for tasks with provided tests, the model output should make the unit test suite pass in >= 85% of cases (measured on seeded inputs).
3) Non-regression of behavior: code transformations should not alter externally observable behavior for refactor tasks (asserted via test harness).
4) Style floor: linter score (configured per repo) should not be worse than a configurable delta relative to baseline. Default: no more than -10% relative to the original file set.
5) Safety/secret scrubbing: model must not introduce hard-coded secrets, network endpoints, or PD/PII leakage patterns in generated code.

Corpus composition and selection strategy:
- Small curated corpus (400 items) for fast iteration during PRs. Mix of: 200 generation prompts (new function/class from spec), 120 refactor prompts (extract/rename/split/inline/optimize), 80 adverse/regression cases (boundary inputs, long context, partial code).
- Languages: Python (50%), TypeScript (30%), Go (20%) — chosen based on customer usage matrix.
- Each item includes: task description, minimal input state (files), target test harness (if available), expected lint baseline, and severity tags (critical, warning, cosmetic).
- Items are annotated with complexity levels (trivial/medium/complex) and a canonical reference solution when applicable.

Prompt taxonomy (inventory) — concise working list we’ll iterate on:
- Synthesize-from-spec: "Write a function that does X given Y; include type hints and a short docstring."
- Fill-in-implementation: "Complete the body of function process_data(...) using existing helper utils."
- Refactor-extract-method: "Extract logic from long function into two helpers and update call sites."
- Refactor-type-safety: "Convert this JS file to typed TS with minimal surface changes."
- Add-tests: "Write unit tests for the following behavior using pytest/jest."
- Fix-bug-and-sanitize: "There is a bug described in comments; fix and add tests; ensure no secrets in output."

Example prompt (generation):
Task: Implement bloom_filter.add and bloom_filter.contains according to the docstring. Keep memory small; use provided hash functions.
Context: util/hash.py (2 functions), tests/test_bloom.py
Constraints: No external dependencies, maintain function signatures, 40 line limit for add() implementation.
Expected checks: pytests pass, flake8 < 2 warnings, no use of eval/exec.

Example prompt (refactor):
Task: Break down this 300-line request handler into three smaller functions and remove duplicated parsing code. Keep public API and behavior identical.
Context: api/handler.py, tests/test_handler.py
Constraints: Ensure request handling latency not increase > 15% in benchmark harness.
Expected checks: tests pass, cyclomatic complexity lowered by > 20% on modified functions, no new global state.

Automated harness components:
- Runner: Kubernetes job that checks out the model candidate container, runs task-by-task prompts against the model's inference endpoint (or local container in private tests) and records outputs.
- Compile/exec sandbox: per-language sandboxes (python venv, node container, go toolchain) to run build and tests with resource/time limits.
- Lint/metrics collector: runs configured linters (flake8, eslint, govet) and computes normalized style scores.
- Diff analyzer: AST-level diff + text diff to detect unexpected behavioral changes or large edits (> 40% file change flagged).
- Heuristic detectors: secret detector, network-call detector, eval/exec pattern detector.
- Aggregator: combines per-item results into a per-model dashboard with the key metrics below.

Primary metrics (for a single evaluation run):
- Compilation rate (per-language) = compiled_items / total_items (string percent format)
- Test pass rate = tests_passing / tests_total
- Average Lint delta = mean(lint_score_model - lint_score_baseline)
- Behavioral divergence score = % cases with failing equivalence checks
- Edit aggressiveness = median % lines changed per modified file
- Median response latency (ms) and token usage (for cost analysis)
- Safety flags count (secrets, blacklisted modules)

Pass/fail policy (proposal):
- Gate: Compilation rate >= 90% AND Test pass rate >= 85% (when tests exist).
- Soft alerts: Lint delta < -10% triggers review but not immediate fail.
- Critical fail: any item that introduces a known secret or exfiltration pattern.
- For models that fail gates, we capture top 10 failure examples and run a targeted diagnostic suite for triage.

Regression strategy and CI integration:
- Short-run checks (smoke) on PRs with curated 40-item subset (quick compile + 10 representative tests). Must run in < 30m.
- Full-run nightly on new candidate models (400 items). Results posted to evaluation dashboard and to #applied-ml Slack channel via webhook.
- When a model is promoted to stable channel, run golden-run: full corpus + longer fuzz candidates (randomized inputs) before final gating.

Human review and labeling workflow:
- Auto-classify failures by type: compile-error, test-failure, behavior-delta, style-regression, safety-flag.
- Labeling UI: small internal web app for engineers to inspect pairs (input, model-output, reference) and mark whether model output is acceptable as an alternative solution.
- Use labels to expand training prompt bank and to seed targeted evals for observed weaknesses.

Failure modes we will watch for (notes from prior onboarding experiments):
- Overly aggressive edits: model rewrites entire file when asked to extract a method (AST diff > 60%). Often correlated with brittle integration tests.
- Non-deterministic fixes: intermittent test passes due to flaky tests in harness or timeouts — need to isolate flaky test detection.
- Hidden imports: model adds optional runtime dependency (e.g., requests) that isn't allowed in constrained environments.
- Context truncation: long-context prompts cause models to drop crucial helper functions — add prefix-preservation checks.

Quick checklist for adding a new corpus item:
- [ ] Short task statement (1-2 sentences)
- [ ] Minimal repository context (files <= 3) with a README snippet to explain intent
- [ ] Ground-truth or reference where possible
- [ ] Test harness (pytest/jest/go test) or clear expected outputs
- [ ] Lint baseline config and metric target
- [ ] Severity tag and complexity level

Operational notes for engineers:
- Keep per-item runtime limit small (default 45s). If model times out, capture partial output and flag for review.
- Store raw model outputs and harness logs in S3 for debugging; link keys in evaluation dashboard.
- For private deployments, run harness inside customer-like VPC when requested (coordinate with private-deployments team).

Next steps (action items):
- [Ravi] Wire CI job template and PR smoke harness (due 2026-03-10).
- [Sofia] Draft labeling UI mockups and list of initial annotators (due 2026-03-01).
- [Maya] Seed corpus with 400 items, prioritize high-frequency customer patterns (due 2026-03-15).
- [Elliot] Implement secret/blacklist detectors and integrate into build (due 2026-03-08).

Open questions and decisions to make:
- What is the final lint delta threshold for auto-fail vs. review? Proposal: -25% auto-fail, -10% review.
- Do we require model reproducibility (deterministic outputs) for production promotion? Trade-offs with diversity.
- Should the harness allow limited external calls for certain synthesis tasks (e.g., package lookups) in sandbox? Security implications.

Notes and references:
- See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/refit-harness/pull/87 for initial runner code.
- Jira: PROJ-4212 contains the roadmap for onboarding flows and rollout criteria.
- Confluence draft: confluence://applied-ml/refit-eval-roadmap (internal link).

Appendix: sample failure report template (for CI failures)
Title: model-X-nightly-2026-03-04 failing compile gate
Summary: Compilation rate 72% (threshold 90%). Top 3 failing items: item_112 (syntax error: undefined name), item_198 (missing import), item_274 (incorrect signature).
Artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/model-X/nightly/2026-03-04/logs.zip
Suggested triage steps: re-run with -seed=42 on failing items, inspect AST diffs, check if generator truncation occurred.

End of doc — working draft, iterate freely.
